rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered non-RSO rental units in Los Angeles may terminate a tenancy only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Landlords may not evict for non-payment unless the tenant owes more than one month's Fair Market Rent, and all eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 6 months' tenancy or lease expiration (whichever first); relocation assistance for no-fault evictions; non-payment eviction only if arrears exceed FMR
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.coverage_text: Covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including single-family dwellings and buildings newer than October 1, 1978. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, some properties owned by HACLA or the government, and units regulated by the RSO.
rules.interaction: The JCO covers units not under the City's RSO. Single-family homes and condominiums that are exempt from state law (AB 1482) can still be covered by the JCO. The page does not say the JCO displaces state law.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases on covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. In Los Angeles the maximum was 8.9% for August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025.
rules.citation: AB 1482 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019); Civil Code Section 1947.12
rules.quoted_span: Previously, from August 1, 2023 to July 31, 2024 the maximum annual increase for units subject to AB 1482 was 8.8%
rules.coverage_text: Buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis; excludes units already subject to the City's RSO.
rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years (rolling); deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties where an owner occupied the other unit for the entire tenancy; single-family homes and condos not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, where the tenant received written notice under Civil Code 1947.12(d)(5)(B)(i); units subject to the City's RSO.
rules.interaction: The JCO does not regulate rent increases. Units subject to the City's RSO are not covered by AB 1482.
